subject: Performance alert: MediSync long-context throughput spike

Subject: High p99 latency starting 09:00 PT - long requests

Hi Marissa —

We started seeing a big jump in p95/p99 for our Hosted API usage around 09:00 PT this morning. This correlates with a batch of long-context requests (32k tokens) that started hitting our production endpoints after a client-side change. Symptoms: 5–15s additional tail latency, a handful of 504s in the last hour, and throughput dropped ~30% on one tenant.

We need immediate help; our clinical workflow depends on sub-second generation for autocomplete. I attached a small request sample and a graph from our side showing p95/p99 spikes.

Can someone confirm whether there's a known regression with long-context handling or any autoscaling backpressure?

Thanks,
Ben Turner

Subject: [Internal] Re: High p99 latency - initial triage notes

Quick triage notes — pulled from our Hosted telemetry for MediSync tenant between 08:45–09:30 PT:
- Spike in p95/p99 strongly correlated with requests that have >24k tokens in the prompt (most at ~32k).
- CPU & GPU utilization on the affected cluster rose ~15%, queue depth increased, and we observed a sharp increase in context KV cache misses for that model family.
- Autoscaler did add pods, but the batching layer slowed due to increased per-request memory pressure; this increased tail latency rather than spreading load effectively.
- We saw ~0.8% 504s (up from baseline ~0.02%).

Mitigation options (fast to slow):
1) Soft-limit: temporarily reject/429 requests greater than 24k tokens for this tenant via routing rule (can be per-tenant, immediate).
2) Model fallback: route >16k requests to a compatible but smaller-context variant optimized for long-window streaming (lower memory but slightly higher per-token cost).
3) Autoscaler tuning: increase GPU mem headroom and change batching thresholds — medium effort (30–90m).
4) Longer-term: kernel-level improvements and KV cache optimizations (days).

I recommend option 1 or 2 as immediate actions; I’ll stand by to implement. Uploading our graphs and a sample trace to the shared drive now.

Attachments uploaded: medisync_p95_p99_graphs.png, request-sample-32k.txt

—Ben C.
Ben Carter
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: High p99 latency starting 09:00 PT - long requests

Ben —

Thanks Ben C. for the quick triage. Ben T, we’re going to push a tenant-level routing rule that rejects requests >24k tokens for 60 minutes while we implement option 2 (model fallback) as a safer alternative. This should reduce the immediate pressure and stop the 504s.

Planned steps (I’ll notify when done):
- 10:15 PT: apply temporary routing rule (reject >24k).
- 10:25 PT: enable model fallback for >16k requests to long-window optimized variant with streaming enabled.
- 11:00 PT: monitor p95/p99 and error rate and decide whether to keep fallback for 24–48h while we perform deeper kernel profiling.

If you prefer a different window or want us to throttle instead of reject, tell us now and we’ll adjust.

—Marissa

Subject: Exec summary & recommended action for MediSync latency spike

Vivek —

Summary: MediSync is experiencing p95/p99 regressions tied to a sudden increase in long-context (24k–32k) requests hitting Hosted. The immediate customer impact is increased latency and a small but visible uptick in 504s. Ben C. has proposed short-term mitigations (tenant-level reject for >24k, or fallback to long-window variant for >16k).

Recommendation (ask for executive sign-off):
- Approve tenant-level fallback to the long-window optimized model for requests >16k for up to 48 hours. This is a conservative step that preserves availability while we profile kernels. Expected trade-offs: slightly higher per-token cost and possible differences in output for edge cases; we will notify MediSync and monitor quality metrics.
- If approved, authorize SRE to keep throttling/429 rule as backup.

I’m attaching the mitigation runbook; Ben C. can execute immediately upon approval. I will draft a brief customer-facing note after approval to set expectations.

Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: runbook-long-context-mitigation.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.co@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance alert: MediSync long-context throughput spike

Ben —

We have approval to proceed with the model fallback for >16k requests and a tenant-level reject for >24k while we monitor. Actions executed:
- 10:16 PT: Applied tenant routing rule rejecting >24k requests (60m).
- 10:26 PT: Enabled fallback routing for requests with token_count >16000 to the long-window variant (lw-cc-32k-optimized).

Early results (10:30–10:50 PT): p95 dropped ~45% from peak and 504s returned to baseline. Our Ops dashboard is in the shared drive (see JIRA INF-4729). We’ll keep the fallback for 24 hours and circle back with a technical postmortem.

We appreciate the quick signal — we’ll follow up with a documented timeline and recommended permanent remediation.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference

A couple of follow-ups we’d like to track:
- Root cause postmortem with kernel/KV cache details and timeline
- A recommended SLA or hard guardrails for customers that send >16k token requests (to avoid surprises)
- A plan for long-term kernel/serving improvements and a rough ETA (days/weeks)

If you can add those items to JIRA INF-4729 that would be great. We’ll plan a short sync next week with Priya and our platform team to review.

Thanks —
Ben
